classification.difficultyReason: Across three quadrilaterals, choose base and corresponding perpendicular height, recognise equal-sided right-angle square, and use familiar Pythagoras for one missing height. All source givens explicitly provided; no proof search.

content.prompt: Find the area of each parallelogram.

spec.description: Four identical side ticks and a right-angle marker define a square. Original lower-right edge is12mm.
spec.mathematics: Four identical side ticks and a right-angle marker define a square. Original lower-right edge is12mm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and meaningful marks; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
All sides are equal and one angle is a right angle, so this is a square.
$$A=12^2=144\text{ mm}^2.$$

spec.description: Rhombus with all four edges equal12mm. Dashed perpendicular across two opposite sides is10mm; the side12mm is the corresponding base.
spec.mathematics: Rhombus with all four edges equal12mm. Dashed perpendicular across two opposite sides is10mm; the side12mm is the corresponding base.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and meaningful marks; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
Use a side of length $12\text{ mm}$ as the base and its perpendicular height $10\text{ mm}$:
$$A=12\times10=120\text{ mm}^2.$$

spec.description: Parallelogram base8mm, oblique side5mm, horizontal right-triangle extension3mm, dashed perpendicular and right-angle marker. Single/double parallel marks retained. Height is not supplied as a new given.
spec.mathematics: Parallelogram base8mm, oblique side5mm, horizontal right-triangle extension3mm, dashed perpendicular and right-angle marker. Single/double parallel marks retained. Height is not supplied as a new given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and meaningful marks; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras, the perpendicular height is
$$h=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4\text{ mm}.$$
Hence $A=8\times4=32\text{ mm}^2$.
